answer: Continuous-use decay pricing. Each agent identity accrues a small copper-denominated holding balance that must be topped up whenever the identity acts; the required top-up rises steeply the faster a single identity transacts, while dormant identities decay toward zero rather than being revoked. New identities start cheap but face a lantern-style slow-charge period before full throughput, so an attacker who spins up N fresh identities on some island of addresses pays N times the entry top-up plus escalating per-action top-ups until each identity seasons,
